Screwdriver Handle Generator

A knurled handle for 1/4" (6.35 mm) hex bits: a socket for the bit with a magnet behind it, storage holes for spare bits, and a screw cap that closes them. Printed upright, the cap separately.
Picking one fills in all settings; changing a setting makes it "Custom".

Handle

The top narrows to the tip, to reach screws in tight spaces. Taper length 0 for none.
The whole length, without the cap's flange. The storage holes take up what the socket and magnet leave (see the summary).

Bit socket

A 1/4" bit is 6.35 mm across flats; the socket is a little wider so the bit slides in. Each corner gets a small round relief of this diameter, centred on the corner: printed corners come out rounded, a bit's are sharp. 0 for none.

Magnet

A closed hexagonal pocket, 0.2 mm higher than the magnet: its flats touch the magnet (flat sides print more accurately than a round hole), plus the clearance on each flat. Pause the print at the height in the summary, drop the magnet in and resume. 0 for no magnet.

Spare bits

Hexagonal holes from the bottom up, each for a stack of bits. They are as long as the handle allows, ending this far below the magnet, so it doesn't hold the topmost spare bits; the summary gives their length and how many 25 mm bits fit (a 100 mm handle: three each).

Screw cap

A rounded 2 mm pitch thread that prints without supports. The clearance is the gap on every side between the cap's thread and the handle's.
The cap's knurled flange is this much larger in radius than the handle, so it is easier to grab (1 mm: a 22 mm handle gets a 24 mm cap). 0: as large as the handle.
Enter dimensions and click Generate.
Shown and saved in print orientation: the handle upright on its bottom end, the cap beside it on its flange. Both are separate objects in the 3MF.
